thread:
leo (sales): Quick heads-up — Podium POC needs a hosted API key for the live demo tomorrow 10am PT. Customer asked specifically that we support mid-demo rotation and quick revocation. Can we provision an ephemeral key and share the rotation playbook?

maya (solutions): We can do an ephemeral key w/ 24h TTL and scoped permissions. Who on Podium needs it (email) and do they need embeddings + generation or just generation? Also, do they want IP allowlisting?

leo (sales): Contact is sam@podium.ai, they need generation + embeddings for the demo. IP allowlist would be helpful but they may demo from multiple locations — prefer a rotation-first approach.

jin (eng): OK — plan: issue ephemeral key labeled `podium-demo` TTL=24h, scopes=generate,embeddings, audit tag=podium-poc. Quick commands below for the ops runbook:

```bash
# create ephemeral token via admin CLI
rw tokens create --label "podium-demo" --scopes generate,embeddings --ttl 24h --tags poc,podium-demo

# revoke token by id (if needed during demo)
rw tokens revoke <token-id>
```

jin (eng): For an in-demo mid-rotation we recommend pre-creating two tokens (active and standby). Swap client config to standby on rotation, then revoke the old one. That avoids a gap.

nina (security): A couple security checks: 1) ensure the token is limited to hosted API (no admin scopes), 2) enable token-use audit logging for the demo window, 3) document the rotation incident flow. If they can't IP lock, we should at least require a short TTL and rotate after demo.

maya (solutions): I'll provision the tokens and share a one-page runbook to Podium with the exact CLI/API calls and a copy/paste curl example. Also will add the steps to rotate without restarting their client: they just update the Authorization header to the standby token.

deploy-bot: Ticket created: POC-583 — ephemeral tokens for Podium demo. Owner: maya. ETA: 2 hours. Link: https://redwood-internal.tickets/POC-583

leo (sales): Perfect. Can we also provide a short-lived dashboard link for them to inspect usage (no cost detail, just request/latency counts)? Helps during demo.

jin (eng): We can create a read-only dashboard view scoped to the token label and share a time-limited link. I'll attach instructions in the runbook.

maya (solutions): Runbook draft (will share to sam@podium.ai):
- create two ephemeral tokens (labels: podium-demo-active, podium-demo-standby)
- configure client to use `podium-demo-active`
- on rotation: update Authorization header to `Bearer <podium-demo-standby>` then revoke the old token via CLI/API
- post-demo: revoke both tokens and archive logs to S3 for 90 days

maya (solutions): curl example for revoke: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/admin/tokens/revoke \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <ADMIN_KEY>" \
  -d '{"token_id":"<token-id>"}'
```

nina (security): Add: require admin key usage to come from a verified internal user (no shared creds) and confirm logs are being forwarded to our SIEM for the demo window.

leo (sales): Thanks — I'll cc legal if we need a short addendum about demo-only access. Can we get the tokens and runbook into sam's inbox by 6pm PT today?

maya (solutions): Yep — provisioning now. I'll post the final runbook and the token metadata here when done.

leo (sales): Awesome — much appreciated.

maya (solutions): Done: created tokens `podium-demo-active` (id: tok_7f9a) and `podium-demo-standby` (id: tok_7f9b). Runbook link: https://redwood-internal.docs/podium-poc-runbook (shared with sam@podium.ai). I also enabled audit-logging for the window.

leo (sales): Got it, forwarding to customer. We'll test rotation at 9:30am PT.

jin (eng): I'll be on standby for any revoke/rotation help.

nina (security): Confirmed SIEM ingestion for logs. Closing on my side.

leo (sales): Thanks team! :thumbsup:
